summary.headline: Kiri Industries Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40% YoY to ₹299 crore, but a ₹57 crore non-cash treasury fair-value loss drove a consolidated loss after tax of ₹39 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹299 crore (up 40% YoY) and consolidated EBITDA was ₹2 crore, with a loss after tax of ₹39 crore before associate income. Management said price increases in H-acid and vinyl cell phone only partly reflected in Q2 because the quarter executed earlier contracted orders, with benefits expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Standalone PAT of ₹248 crore for H1 was supported by Q1 treasury gains, and Q2 was hit by the same unrealised treasury loss. Management reiterated that the copper fertilizer project's phase one remains on track for H1 FY28.

segments.name: Dyes and dye intermediates (standalone plus Dystar India JV)
segments.commentary: Management said about 95% of intermediates are consumed captively; intermediate capacity utilisation is below 60%. Dye sales are the core business, with at least 50% exported and a 2-3 month order book.

segments.name: Associates (Longshan Keri and another, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Contributed ₹16 crore in Q2 and about ₹37 crore in H1 FY27 to profit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 and Q4 FY27 to show significantly higher dye performance than Q1 and Q2 as price increases flow through with a one-to-two-quarter lag.
Dye demand is expected to stay stable through H2 FY27, supported by textile sector activity.
H-acid prices have been ₹1,600-1,800/kg for three to four weeks; management expects the H-acid price to stabilise around calendar 2027 as Chinese continuous nitration capacity comes back.
Copper fertilizer project phase one is on track to commence in H1 FY28; Makilala mine output of ~140,000 t copper concentrate expected by FY28-29, about 6-7% of the 1.6 million t requirement.
Around 80% of copper raw material requirement is said to be secured through sourcing visibility following LME Week.
capex_capacity: Integrated copper and fertilizer project: equipment deliveries have begun, and foundation and structural works are progressing across key units; dedicated jetty, desalination and raw material handling systems are under development.
Downstream copper units total about 2.6 lakh tonnes capacity, to be operational alongside the smelting complex in FY28-29.

Acquired 40% stake in Makilala Mining (Philippines) during the quarter; Kiri may need slightly over $40 million as its equity share of capex, with the balance funded by debt. Capex is still under evaluation.
Intermediate capacity utilisation is below 60%; management is working to raise output over the next 2-3 months.
demand_pricing: H-acid prices were about ₹400-500/kg for almost five years before the recent hike and are now ₹1,600-1,800/kg. Management attributes this to Chinese H-acid capacity cuts after a continuous-nitration regulation, which limits Chinese output to under 50,000 t against about 100,000 t of annual demand.
Vinyl sulphone (VS) prices are above ₹450/kg, but input costs (sulphur, naphthalene, caustic, methanol) have risen sharply, so margin gains have been limited.
Reactive dye prices are about ₹1,500-1,600/kg, moving with intermediates after a two-to-three-month lag.
Management said the H-acid price increase reflects the Chinese supply gap and that Indian H-acid is exported to China.
Peers earn higher margins than Kiri's 8-10% range; management pointed to the lag between input price changes and dye realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Dystar JV and consolidated results remain weak, with a PBT loss of about ₹7 crore even after the H-acid price rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier, lower-priced orders were still being executed, so the price rise will show in Q3 and Q4. Legal expenses for the Philippine mines were below ₹3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri take an operational role at Makilala Mining, given its 40% minority stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiri has board-level participation and helped select the new management, including a CEO from Carbon Copper. Kiri's Philippine subsidiary is operating. The Philippine court appeal on the arbitration award is pending.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Chinese H-acid supply disruption last, and what does it mean for costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects disruption through the end of FY27 and prices to stabilise around calendar 2027 at a level above the old range. Indian and Chinese raw material costs are at parity, so Chinese costs are not expected to rise structurally.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri shift to selling intermediates as a main product?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Dyes are the primary business. Over 90-95% of intermediates are consumed captively, and spot sales of intermediates are opportunistic only.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from the dye business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is ₹1,300-1,500 crore in top line, with all sales reported as dye sales and captive consumption above 95%.

qa_highlights.question: How will copper price moves affect the new project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the copper business earns a constant LME spread, and purchases and sales are fully hedged through a dedicated desk, so the project is insulated from price moves.

risks_watch: Q2 treasury fair-value loss of ₹57 crore; reported profit depends heavily on treasury marks.
Whether the Q3 and Q4 FY27 price pass-through is realised, given the two-to-three-month lag and dependence on China's regulatory recovery.
Makilala Mining: Philippine appeal on the arbitration award and a minority-stake governance structure.
Copper cathode supply constraints (Japan duty-free) and the blended cost of imported cathode.
Dependence on Chinese capacity restoration, which could erode H-acid margins from calendar 2027.
Project capex and funding for the copper fertilizer complex, with equity and debt split still under evaluation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook for H-acid and dyes and on the copper project, but cautious on near-term profitability, which management ties to a lagged price pass-through. Answers to margin and intermediate-sales questions were repetitive and partly evasive, and the promoter's appeal to investors was personal rather than data-driven.
key_quotes: So the reason why you see the profits comparatively lower is because of the earlier quarters and earlier orders which are being executed mainly pertaining to Dys.
Selling dyes is a long term business as a long term phenomena for the company while selling intermediates is not a long term business model for the company.
The project remains on track for phase one commencing in first half FY 2028.

adds.what: Integrated copper and fertilizer project phase one (smelting complex) with downstream copper units totalling about 2.6 lakh t capacity

growth.why: Management guides significantly higher dye performance in Q3-Q4 FY27 as H-acid and VS price increases flow through with a 1-2 quarter lag, backed by contracted orders and price data but no volume or revenue number; copper phase one is held for H1 FY28 with equipment deliveries begun.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides significantly higher dye performance in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as H-acid (₹400-500/kg to ₹1,600-1,800/kg) and VS price rises flow through with a 1-2 quarter lag, though Q2 material margin rose to 29.1% from 26.4% and standalone EBITDA margin was only 2.4%, with input costs rising sharply.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Copper and fertilizer project phase one is under construction with equipment deliveries begun and management reiterating a start in H1 FY28, alongside about 2.6 lakh t of downstream copper units due in FY28-29.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Intermediate utilisation is below 60%, and management is working to raise output over 2-3 months, but dye demand is only expected to be stable through H2 FY27 with no volume number given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Makilala Mining capex (Kiri's equity share slightly over $40 million, balance debt) is still under evaluation, and the capex split is unresolved, though utilisation is low so no new capacity beyond the copper project is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects significantly higher dye performance in Q3 and Q4 versus Q1 and Q2, and H-acid prices of ₹1,600-1,800/kg are well above the old ₹400-500/kg range, but the uplift is unquantified and depends on pass-through lag.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 consolidated EBITDA was only ₹2 crore and the PBT loss persisted, with the Q3-Q4 pass-through dependent on a 1-2 quarter lag and on China's regulatory recovery, which could erode H-acid margins from calendar 2027.

rows.label: Contracted orders at old prices executing through Q2
rows.why: Earlier lower-priced contracts were still being executed in Q2, so the H-acid and VS price rise shows up in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as the backlog rolls over, with dye order book at 2-3 months.

rows.label: Makilala Mining arbitration appeal pending
rows.why: The Philippine court appeal on the arbitration award is pending, and Kiri holds only a 40% minority stake with legal expenses below ₹3 crore in the quarter.

rows.label: Chinese H-acid supply gap persists to FY27-end
rows.why: Chinese output is under 50,000 t against about 100,000 t demand, with management expecting disruption through end-FY27 and prices stabilising around calendar 2027 above the old range.

tone.note: Management was confident on H-acid pricing, dyes and the copper project timeline, but cautious on near-term profitability tied to the lagged pass-through; analysts pushed on margins, intermediate sales and the Makilala governance and capex split, and answers were repetitive.
